Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for HydroGlass launch

Rishi —

Thanks for taking this. We have an internal launch window the week of Nov 16th and need a dedicated capacity plan that guarantees p95 inference latency <= 220ms for our primary customer flows. A few details up front:

- Workload profile: 70% short queries (avg 120 tokens in, 80 tokens out), 25% standard (450 tokens in, 320 out), 5% long (1.2k tokens in/out for batch analytics).
- Expected peak concurrency: 420 concurrent users at launch; burst-to-peak factor 2.2 for campaign spikes.
- Baseline SLA: p95 <= 220ms; p99 target is negotiable but we'd like to understand tail risk.
- Region: primary in us-west with a fallback us-east.

I've attached a CSV export of our expected request distribution and some telemetry from our pilot. Can you confirm tokens/sec (aggregate) we should commit, recommended GPU slab sizing (gpus/node and instance count), and how much headroom Redwood recommends for safe operation during the first 90 days? Also flag any quantization/model variants you'd recommend to meet the SLO.

Appreciate a quick estimate — procurement wants a target commit number for the contract draft this week.

—Alex
Alex Li
VP Product, HydroGlass

Alex —

Thanks — got the profile and the pilot CSV. Quick take below (high-level estimates so procurement has something to work with today). I'll follow up with a short model mapping and a capacity workbook by end of day tomorrow.

Summary (initial):
- Estimated steady-state tokens/sec (aggregate): ~68k tps (tokens/sec) across all traffic classes at current concurrency assumptions.
- Peak tokens/sec with 2.2x marketing spike: ~150k tps.
- Recommended committed TPS for contract (90-day conservative): 100k tps (this balances cost and headroom while allowing safe burst to 150k via dedicated burst pool).
- GPU slab recommendation: 1. Dedicated pool sized for 100k tps using 40 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (example: 10 nodes x 4 gpus) configured with mixed precision + KV-cache warmup; a 12-GPU buffer (30% operating headroom) provisioned for peak absorbing and graceful degradation policies.

SLO/latency notes:
- To hit p95 <= 220ms we need aggressive KV caching for short queries and batching for standard queries. Long analytic requests should be routed to a separate backplane (long-job workers) to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Quantization (8-bit with dynamic-matmul where possible) will reduce memory footprint and increase throughput but requires validation on model fidelity. Recommend a split: production primary on FP16-optimized variant and a quantized variant as fallback for cost-sensitive lanes.

Deliverables planned:
- Camila will run a short tokens->TPS mapping with three workload samples and attach an explicit GPU mapping (gpus/node, nodes required) in the capacity workbook.
- Kimberly will produce a headroom sensitivity table (0%, 15%, 30% buffer) and an ops playbook for autoscaling/burst usage.

For procurement: if you need a single commit number now, propose commit = 100k tps with a documented burst policy allowing short-term absorption up to 150k tps (billed/credited per usage).

Rishi

Rishi / Camila / Alex —

Attached is the capacity workbook (high-level XLS tabbed) with the mappings referenced in Rishi's note. Key excerpts below so everyone has the numbers without opening the sheet:

- Baseline mapping assumptions: average token processing cost per token = 0.000012 GPU-seconds (FP16 runtime on our inference engine); quantized runtime reduces to ~0.000008 GPU-seconds for standard layers, but increases CPU postprocessing by ~8ms.

- Token-to-GPU conversion (point estimate):
  * 100k tps sustained -> ~36 aggregate GPU-seconds/sec -> with A100-80GB equivalent (1 gpu = 1 GPU-second/sec) you need ~36 GPUs continuous.
  * Add 30% headroom -> 47 GPUs -> round to 48 GPUs (12 nodes x 4 gpus) for operational comfort.

- Burst handling:
  * For 150k tps peak: 54 GPU-seconds/sec -> with burst pool and pre-warmed KV caches we recommend a short-burst pool of 12 additional GPUs (fast warmup policy).

- Latency fit (p95):
  * With 48 GPUs + KV caching split (short-queries served from cache tier), expected p95: ~190ms.
  * With FP16 only (no quantization), p95 drift to ~205–230ms under high standard-query fraction; adding the quantized fallback keeps tail risk within contract if fidelity checks pass.

- Operational recommendations:
  * Canary rollout: start production on 60% traffic to the dedicated pool for 72 hours, monitor p95 and error-rate.
  * Cold-start policy: persistent KV cache warming during business hours and pre-warm on scheduled marketing spikes (pre-bake flows 30–60 minutes).

Attachments: hydroglass_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)

I'll hand the spreadsheet to Camila to produce the formal workbook rows for procurement (costing per-month by committed TPS and overspend rules).

—Kimberly
